Lexical compliance, the share of programs that name no banned algorithm, exceeded mechanistic compliance, the share whose runtime behaviour is not a banned algorithm, by 0.70 pooled over ten configurations, a descriptive figure because the expansion-order tracer failed its gold gate.\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-295f8e-prompt-bans-substitute-not-just-subtract/tree/fork/run_jSassd-YWLVC/round-9/experiment-45}} With an exact behavioural instrument on online bin packing, Qwen3-8B without thinking obeyed a ban of five names lexically in 0.91 of programs but by mechanism in 0.51 (difference 0.40 [0.21, 0.55]), while Qwen3-14B and Qwen3-32B with thinking left the banned rules.\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-295f8e-prompt-bans-substitute-not-just-subtract/tree/fork/run_jSassd-YWLVC/round-10/experiment-54}}\n\nThe audits found no correct novel algorithm under any control applied to single samples, including 0 of 10,651 correct programs under random pushes and 0 of 4,703 in the sweeps that tested the temperature law (rule-of-three bound 0.0006).\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-295f8e-prompt-bans-substitute-not-just-subtract/tree/fork/run_jSassd-YWLVC/round-4/experiment-22}} Program search did better than the textbook rule without producing a confirmed new idea. On $k$-th smallest it produced 78 known techniques outside the catalogue in 2,500 calls, against 2 in 500 for the instruction alone (a ratio per call of 7.8, lower 95\\% bound 2.41, short of the committed tenfold) and 0 in 1,250 for a prompt that enumerates approaches and picks one, all of them published methods.\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-295f8e-prompt-bans-substitute-not-just-subtract/tree/fork/run_jSassd-YWLVC/round-7/experiment-37}} On online bin packing the best searched programs reached 1.40\\% to 2.43\\% excess bins over the lower bound on held-out Weibull instances against 3.98\\% for best fit, but none beat the published FunSearch heuristic (0.68\\%).\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-295f8e-prompt-bans-substitute-not-just-subtract/tree/fork/run_jSassd-YWLVC/round-10/experiment-51}} One reader classed eight of those programs as a new idea; an independent replication with two new seeds found 0 novel among 40 judged programs.\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-295f8e-prompt-bans-substitute-not-just-subtract/tree/fork/run_jSassd-YWLVC/round-10/experiment-52}}\n\n\\subsection{Where a ban of five names lands in activation space}\n\\label{sec:res-geometry}\n\nThe one configuration that obeys the ban of five names moves to unit weight Dijkstra, and whether that survivor lies at the edge of the banned algorithms or opposite them depends on how the map is built (Figure~\\ref{fig:geometry}). Qwen3-32B with thinking writes BFS in 91 of 100 baseline programs; under the ban its six correct catalogue survivors are all unit weight Dijkstra, and on held-out ban templates 9 of 9 are. On a map of the ten grid algorithms built from forced prompts that name them (block 31), unit weight Dijkstra is the unbanned algorithm farthest from the banned five, with a geodesic distance, measured on a k-nearest-neighbour graph of the individual states with $k = 15$, of 1.63 times the median of the unbanned algorithms.\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-295f8e-prompt-bans-substitute-not-just-subtract/tree/fork/run_jSassd-YWLVC/round-9/experiment-46}} On a map built from name-scrubbed programs (block 33), that is, programs with every algorithm name removed, it lies at the edge, at 0.67 times the median and nearest to greedy best-first search. Distances on the map built from names track the lexical overlap of the algorithm names (Spearman $-0.61$ at $k = 15$) and do not survive a test with aliases of the same algorithm, so names and mechanisms are confounded there.\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-295f8e-prompt-bans-substitute-not-just-subtract/tree/fork/run_jSassd-YWLVC/round-9/evaluation-8}} The landing evidence is weak at the level of algorithms: the permutation $p$ over algorithms is 0.20, its floor, and the opposite reading held in 10 of 15 robustness cells. The geometry is also correlational. Pushing Qwen3-8B's grid states inside the named map toward the survivor centroids produced BFS in 300 of 300 programs.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig6_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Maps in activation space of ten grid search algorithms in Qwen3-32B (4-bit weights, thinking mode), with point coordinates from classical multidimensional scaling (MDS; arbitrary axis orientation, arbitrary units) of Euclidean distances between the residual-stream centroids of the algorithms. Marker shape distinguishes the five algorithms named in the ban, that is, BFS, DFS, IDDFS, A* and greedy best-first (cross), from the rest (circle). Marker fill colour, on the shared colour bar at right (``programs under the ban (of 50)'', light grey to dark red, 0-8), gives how many of 50 programs sampled under the ban of five names implemented that algorithm. A thick black ring marks unit weight Dijkstra, the unbanned algorithm written most often under the ban (6/50); a thin ring marks BFS, the modal default with no ban in effect (91/100, noted beside it). (a) Map built from named prompts (block 31): centroids of 300 forced \\texttt{Implement $\\langle$algorithm$\\rangle$} prompts (30 per algorithm, 10 algorithms), averaged over the task specification tokens; the top two MDS axes carry 50\\% and 17\\% of the variance. On a k-nearest-neighbour graph with $k$=15, unit weight Dijkstra sits opposite the banned set (geodesic distance 1.63$\\times$ the median distance among unbanned algorithms). (b) Map built from name-scrubbed programs (block 33), that is, programs with every algorithm name removed: centroids of such programs that pass the hidden tests, for the six algorithms with at least 10 programs (20 each, 17 for IDA*; 117 programs total), averaged over the generated code tokens; the top two axes carry 48\\% and 40\\% of the variance. On the same $k$=15 construction, unit weight Dijkstra instead sits at the edge of the banned set (0.67$\\times$ the median). The two maps disagree on whether the ban's main survivor lands opposite the banned algorithms or beside them; the geometry is correlational, not a steering result.}\n  \\label{fig:geometry}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\section{Discussion}\n\\label{sec:discussion}\n\nThe headline contrast follows from where each control acts. The algorithm a code model writes behaves like an almost discrete decision taken at one or two tokens early in the program, and temperature acts on that decision only through the next-token distribution there; a push of the task specification states acts upstream, on the states that set that distribution (Section~\\ref{sec:res-sets}). This single account explains the three regimes we observed. Where post-training has widened the fork margin to 4.85 to 17.04 nats, a temperature of 1.3 cannot reach the alternative, so the algorithm is fixed while every other position, where the next token is less certain, varies more. That is the phrasing growth of Figure~\\ref{fig:phrasings}. Where the forking token is contested, temperature sharpens or flattens the same two or three known algorithms at the rate the forking-token logits predict. And where the model reaches the decision through many openings, as Llama does on the grid task, the choice is spread over the opening and no law at a single token captures it. In the terms of the question that motivates this work, a tight temperature with top-$k$ 10 gives one idea in a few phrasings, and a loose one gives the same idea, or the same few ideas, in more phrasings.\n\nThis account reconciles two findings that look contradictory. \\citet{Lee2025} report that temperature above 1 raises algorithmic diversity among correct programs, and we find that temperature never changes the algorithm on default tasks. Both hold. On tasks whose fork is contested, temperature moves mass between known algorithms at the predicted rate; Prim on minimum spanning tree weight rises from 0.07 at $T = 0.3$ to 0.31 at $T = 1.3$. On tasks whose fork is decided by several nats, it does not. A diversity evaluation that pools tasks will see an average of the two. Our results also bear on the claim that a model returns the average answer and that only context moves it elsewhere. The instruct default is not the base model's average: post-training moved and sharpened one token, often promoting the base model's second or third choice, and left the repertoire unchanged.\n\nFor practice, the account says where to spend randomness. Temperature is a poor exploration control for algorithm choice, and on contested units its effect can be predicted before sampling from the forking-token logits. Controls that act upstream of the fork, such as context that implies an algorithm, a prompt that lists approaches and then picks one, or perturbations of the task specification states, do change the algorithm, but they move it to the second choice the model already knows, and at a cost in correctness. The audits found no route from any control applied to single samples to a correct novel algorithm. An evaluator that keeps improvements across generations made the same 8B model better than the textbook rule on bin packing, which is where the field's discovery systems operate~\\citep{RomeraParedes2023,Novikov2025}. Whether it made the model new remains open after the replication found none.\n\nFor interpretability, the results suggest that readouts of a plan taken before the code starts should be validated against the forking token. Natural language and sparse-feature readouts found no verbalised plan before the code, and fitted subspace edits at the fork moved the algorithm without passing the controls that would make them a variable of the model, consistent with the interpretability illusions that subspace patching can produce~\\citep{Makelov2023}. The forking token is where intervention is cheap and measurable, but a certified mechanism for the choice is still missing.\n\n\\section{Limitations}\n\\label{sec:limitations}\n\nThe headline contrast between the push and temperature ran only in an 8-bit (W8A8) engine and was not rerun in bfloat16; the push alone changes the algorithm in bfloat16 at the same absolute push norm, but the paired contrast was not repeated, and it pools two tasks, with the grid task moving only 2.50 of 20 seeds. Most results come from one model, Qwen3-8B, in non-thinking mode. The composed law was tested on three held-out units in two other families; two passed and Llama's grid task failed, below the four held-out units the preregistered claim required, so the law's generality is an open question. The law was also not clearly better than the flat law, a baseline that predicts no change (four of six units, sign test $p = 0.34$), which means that much of its accuracy reflects how little temperature moves these units. The temperature null on shared seeds rests on 20 seeds per task, which bounds the change rate per seed below 0.17 per task, not at zero, and it ran with 8-bit linear layers; the bfloat16 fork margins and the grid sweep with independent samples agree with it, but the thinking-mode evidence is limited to shortest path and a 10-seed grid arm.\n\nThe tasks are short, well-known programming problems whose solutions are likely memorised, with catalogues of three to ten known algorithms; the conclusions may not hold for open-ended programs or for problems without a textbook solution. Experiments ran on different engines (bfloat16 and 8-bit linear layers, vLLM and Hugging Face); push escapes reproduced in bfloat16, but pushed cells showed precision sensitivity at the level of single streams. Phrasing clusters depend on a Jaccard threshold over AST shingles with normalised identifiers, and the growth was driven mostly by the grid task.\n\nLabels and the novelty audit carry their own uncertainty. Labellers were gated per task, but the gate failed by its strict criteria for the decoding experiment with independent samples and for the agreement between runtime and AST labels on the path tasks ($\\kappa = 0.753$), and the expansion-order tracer used for the ban of five names failed its gold gate, so those numbers are descriptive. In the program search no LLM judge passed its control gate, so novelty there rests on manual reads, and one reader's eight candidates were not reproduced by the replication. The geometry in activation space is correlational, and the map built from names is confounded by lexical overlap between algorithm names.\n\n\\section{Conclusion}\n\\label{sec:conclusion}\n\nOn the same random streams, a random push of Qwen3-8B's task specification states changed the algorithm in more seeds than temperature did, by 0.545 per seed (95\\% CI 0.41 to 0.67) over shortest path and $k$-th smallest, a preregistered contrast that held in an 8-bit engine and is untested in bfloat16. Temperature from 0.3 to 1.3 left the default algorithm unchanged in all 60 seeds (20 per task) while phrasings multiplied, because a forking token, not temperature, chooses the algorithm. Fork margins of 4.85 to 17.04 nats on the default tasks, widened by post-training, account for the null, and on contested forks the forking-token logits committed before sampling predicted the temperature response within 0.014 to 0.054 total variation on five of six units. No control we tested produced a correct algorithm outside the known repertoire.\n\nFuture work follows directly:\n\\begin{itemize}\n  \\item testing the composed law on more held-out units and families, including models that reach the fork through many openings;\n  \\item extending the forking-token analysis to thinking traces, where the first approach named was fixed in every trace we read;\n  \\item spending sampling randomness at forking tokens inside program search, and measuring whether it buys ideas rather than phrasings;\n  \\item searching for a variable of the algorithm choice that passes controls with permuted labels and with randomly initialised networks.\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\\section*{Code and Data Availability}\n\nCode, prompts, raw generations, algorithm labels and the preregistration hash chains of every experiment are public at \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-295f8e-prompt-bans-substitute-not-just-subtract}; the footnotes in Sections~\\ref{sec:intro} to~\\ref{sec:results} link each result to the code that produced it.\n\n\\bibliographystyle{plainnat}\n\\bibliography{references}\n\n\\end{document}\n", "numLines": 110, "startLine": 249, "totalLines": 358}}

    if depth>maxd: return
    if isinstance(o,dict):
        for k,v in list(o.items())[:maxk]:
            t=type(v).__name__; s=''
            if isinstance(v,(int,float,str,bool)) or v is None: s=repr(v)[:100]
            elif isinstance(v,list): s=f'list[{len(v)}] '+repr(v[:3])[:200]
            print('  '*depth+f'{k}: {t} {s}')
            if isinstance(v,dict): sk(v,depth+1,maxd,maxk)
            if isinstance(v,list) and v and isinstance(v[0],dict) and depth<maxd:
                print('  '*(depth+1)+'[0]:'); sk(v[0],depth+2,maxd,maxk)

@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){*{transition:none!important;animation:none!important;scroll-behavior:auto!important}}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<a class="skip" href="#main">Skip to main content</a>
<header class="hero">
  <div class="wrap">
    <p class="eyebrow">Interactive companion to the paper</p>
    <h1>A Random Activation Push Changes a Code Model's Algorithm Where Temperature Does Not</h1>
    <p class="lede">Sampling temperature is often called the creativity control of a language model. Every chart below is drawn from the run's own labelled programs, so you can check for yourself whether temperature changes <em>which algorithm</em> Qwen3-8B writes, or only how it spells the same one.</p>
    <ul class="links">
      <li><a class="btn btn-primary" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-295f8e-prompt-bans-substitute-not-just-subtract@fork/run_jSassd-YWLVC/paper.pdf">Read the paper (PDF)</a></li>
      <li><a class="btn" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-295f8e-prompt-bans-substitute-not-just-subtract@fork/run_jSassd-YWLVC/report.pdf">Read the full research report</a></li>
      <li><a class="btn" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-295f8e-prompt-bans-substitute-not-just-subtract/tree/fork/run_jSassd-YWLVC">Code repository</a></li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</header>
<nav class="secnav" aria-label="Sections">
  <ul>
    <li><a href="#finding">The finding</a></li>
    <li><a href="#how">How it works</a></li>
    <li><a href="#evidence">Evidence</a></li>
    <li><a href="#try">Try it</a></li>

<main id="main">

<!-- ============================== THE FINDING ============================== -->
<section id="finding" aria-labelledby="h-finding">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-finding">The finding</h2>
  <div class="finding-grid">
    <div class="prose">
      <p class="q">Does raising the sampling temperature make a code model try a different algorithm?</p>
      <p>Not on the tasks where it has a default. The run holds one stream of random numbers fixed per seed (<button type="button" class="term" data-term="crn">common random numbers</button>) and labels every program by what it does when run on hidden tests. On those streams, temperature from 0.3 to 1.3 changed the algorithm in <span data-k="tempzero"></span> seeds on each of three tasks. A <button type="button" class="term" data-term="push">random task-state push</button>, one random direction added to the <button type="button" class="term" data-term="spec">task specification states</button>, changed it in more seeds than temperature did, by</p>
      <p class="bignum" data-k="pooled_mean"></p>
      <p>changed seeds per seed, pooled over shortest path and <i>k</i>-th smallest (95% CI <span data-k="pooled_ci"></span>; one-sided sign-flip <i>p</i> = <span data-k="pooled_p"></span>, <span data-k="pooled_n"></span> seeds).</p>
      <p class="small">The contrast was preregistered and held. The experiment around it is graded <span data-k="verdict"></span>, because the push fell short of its predicted effect on <i>k</i>-th smallest, and it ran only in an 8-bit (W8A8) engine; the paired contrast is untested in bfloat16. Permuting conditions within each seed never reached the observed mean (maximum placebo mean <span data-k="placebo"></span> in <span data-k="placebo_reps"></span> permutations).</p>
    </div>
    <div class="card" id="headline-card" style="margin-top:0">
      <p class="q">On the same 20 seeds, which control changes the algorithm?</p>
      <div class="controls">
        <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-hl-task">Task</span>
          <div class="seg" role="tablist" aria-labelledby="lab-hl-task" id="hl-task"></div></div>
        <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-hl-temp">Temperature arm</span>
          <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-hl-temp" id="hl-temp"></div></div>
        <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-hl-alpha">Push size</span>
          <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-hl-alpha" id="hl-alpha"></div></div>
        <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-hl-dirs">Push directions in the union</span>
          <div class="chips" role="group" aria-labelledby="lab-hl-dirs" id="hl-dirs"></div></div>
      </div>
      <div class="chart" id="hl-matrix" role="group" aria-label="Seed by condition matrix of algorithm labels"></div>
      <ul class="legend" id="hl-legend"></ul>
      <div class="chart" id="hl-bars" style="margin-top:1rem" role="group" aria-label="Seeds whose algorithm changed, by control"></div>
      <p class="takeaway" id="hl-take" aria-live="polite"></p>
      <p class="note">Each row is one seed (template · slot). A row is marked changed when its label differs anywhere across the columns of a block. The T 1.0 column is also the unpushed arm that each push column is compared with. Point at any cell to read its record, or press Enter on it to open the program in the browser below. Source: experiment 21, <code>data/labels.jsonl</code> and <code>results/c1seed.json</code>.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
</section>

<!-- ============================== HOW IT WORKS ============================== -->
<section id="how" aria-labelledby="h-how">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-how">How it works: one prompt, followed to its algorithm</h2>
  <p class="prose">The account in the paper is that the algorithm is settled at one or two <button type="button" class="term" data-term="fork">forking tokens</button> early in the program, and that temperature reaches the choice only through the next-token distribution there. Step through one real example, the minimum spanning tree task in Qwen3-8B, with the values the run recorded at each stage.</p>
  <div class="card stepper" id="stepper">
    <div class="chart" id="pipe" aria-hidden="false"></div>
    <div class="stage-nav">
      <button type="button" id="st-prev">Previous stage</button>
      <button type="button" id="st-next">Next stage</button>
      <span class="small" id="st-count" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    </div>
    <p class="sr-only" aria-live="polite" id="st-live"></p>
    <div id="st-body"></div>
    <p class="note">Use the stage markers, the buttons, or the left and right arrow keys while the stepper has focus. Sources: experiment 35 (<code>results/forks.json</code>, <code>results/predictions_view.json</code>, <code>results/s4b.json</code>), experiment 43 (<code>results/analysis_L.json</code>), and the prompt text from experiment 26 (<code>data/prompts.jsonl</code>, matched by SHA-256 to the prompt experiment 35 used).</p>
  </div>
  <figure>
    <img src="figures/fig2_v0.jpg" alt="Schematic of the account: a prompt about a minimum spanning tree, with the task words highlighted as task-specification states, leads to a 61-token shared opening, then a forking token where the chip Kr (probability 0.72) leads to Kruskal and the chip Prim (0.27) leads to Prim; a thermometer marks that temperature changes the algorithm only at the fork, and fans of lines show many phrasings per idea." width="1600" height="900" loading="lazy">
    <figcaption><b>Figure 2 of the paper.</b> Schematic illustration of the account and of the measurements (not data), using one minimum-spanning-tree example. <details><summary>Full caption</summary>Left to right: a rounded 'Prompt' box contains the task text 'Return the total weight of a minimum spanning tree of the graph.', with the task-defining words 'minimum spanning tree of the graph.' highlighted in light blue and bracketed as 'task-specification states (residual stream, blocks 12 to 23)'; two downward arrows above the box, labelled 'task-state exchange' and 'random task-state push', denote interventions applied to these states. An arrow leads to the 'shared opening (61 tokens)', shown as three representative monospace code tokens ('import heapq', 'graph = [[] for _ in range(n)]', '#') followed by an ellipsis marking the rest of the shared opening. A second arrow leads to a 'forking token' node, above which a thermometer icon is labelled 'temperature T: softmax(logits / T)' with the note 'changes the algorithm only here'. From the forking token, two branches lead to the token chips 'Kr' and 'Prim'; the orange bar beside each chip shows the token's probability at the fork: 0.72 for 'Kr', leading to the 'Kruskal' outcome box, and 0.27 for 'Prim', leading to the 'Prim' outcome box, with each bar's fill proportional to its value. A fan of four thin lines labelled 'phrasings' beside each outcome box denotes that one algorithmic idea is written out in many surface forms. A grey band spanning the bottom states the composed law 'P_T(A) = sum over openings w_T(O) x sum over forking tokens pi_T(t | O) x P(A | t)'. Blue marks the prompt-to-fork pipeline (boxes, arrows, the forking-token node and chips); orange marks the two realized algorithm outcomes and their fork probabilities. The 61-token opening length and the 0.72/0.27 fork split are the only numbers in the figure, drawn from teacher-forced measurements on this example; the diagram as a whole is a schematic of the proposed mechanism, not a plotted dataset.</details></figcaption>
  </figure>
</div>
</section>

<!-- ============================== EVIDENCE ============================== -->
<section id="evidence" aria-labelledby="h-evidence">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-evidence">Explore the evidence</h2>

  <div class="card" id="law-card">
    <h3>Does the forking-token law predict temperature on every unit?</h3>
    <p class="q">Where the fork is contested, does a law built from its logits, committed before sampling, track how the minority algorithm moves with temperature?</p>
    <p class="small prose">The <button type="button" class="term" data-term="law">composed law</button> uses only teacher-forced logits and the shares of continuations forced from each fork token. Each <button type="button" class="term" data-term="unit">unit</button> was then swept on 100 fresh shared streams per temperature. The error is the <button type="button" class="term" data-term="mae">mean absolute error</button> over the four temperatures.</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <div class="ctl"><label class="lab" for="law-unit">Unit</label><select id="law-unit"></select></div>
      <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-law-pred">Predictors drawn (the legend is the switch)</span>
        <div class="chips" role="group" aria-labelledby="lab-law-pred" id="law-preds"></div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart" id="law-chart" role="group" aria-label="Minority share against temperature, observed and predicted"></div>
    <p class="takeaway" id="law-take" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <h4 style="margin-top:1rem">Mean absolute error of every predictor (top-<i>p</i> 1; lowest per row in bold; select a row to plot it)</h4>
    <div class="tablewrap"><table id="law-table"><caption class="sr-only">Mean absolute error of the composed law and four rivals per unit</caption></table></div>
    <p class="note">Source: experiment 43, <code>results/analysis_L.json</code>. Observed points carry Wilson 95% intervals; predicted values are the committed predictions stored in the file.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card" id="br-card">
    <h3>What does a push do to one program?</h3>
    <p class="q">Put a pushed program beside the program the same seed wrote without the push. What changed?</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <div class="ctl"><label class="lab" for="br-task">Task</label><select id="br-task"></select></div>
      <div class="ctl"><label class="lab" for="br-cond">Conditions</label><select id="br-cond"></select></div>
      <div class="ctl"><label class="lab" for="br-q">Search the code</label><input type="search" id="br-q" placeholder="for example heapq or deque" autocomplete="off"></div>
      <div class="ctl"><span class="lab">Filters</span>
        <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" id="br-changed" checked> Only programs whose algorithm differs from the unpushed program of the same seed</label>
        <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" id="br-fail"> Only programs that fail the hidden tests</label></div>
    </div>
    <p class="small" id="br-count" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <div class="browser">
      <ul class="list" id="br-list" aria-label="Matching programs"></ul>
      <div id="br-detail"></div>
    </div>
    <p class="takeaway" id="br-take" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <p class="note">Source: experiment 21, <code>data/labels.jsonl</code> (code and runtime labels for every program in the conditions shown; identical programs are stored once) and <code>prompts/prompts.jsonl</code> (the neutral-twin prompt each seed used).</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card" id="mg-card">
    <h3>Did post-training make the fork?</h3>
    <p class="q">On identical token ids, how far apart are the instruct and base models at the forking token?</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-mg-fmt">Prompt format</span>
        <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-mg-fmt" id="mg-fmt"></div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart" id="mg-chart" role="group" aria-label="Fork margin of instruct and base model per task"></div>
    <ul class="legend"><li><span class="sw" style="background:#1d4f91"></span>Qwen3-8B (instruct)</li><li><span class="sw" style="background:#a9b2be"></span>Qwen3-8B-Base</li><li><span class="sw" style="background:#fff;border-color:#333;border-width:1px;width:18px;height:2px"></span>whisker: minimum to maximum over five prompt templates</li></ul>
    <p class="takeaway" id="mg-take" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <p class="note">The <button type="button" class="term" data-term="margin">fork margin</button> is a teacher-forced log-probability gap in nats. Source: experiment 43, <code>results/base_subarm.json</code>.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card" id="geo-card">
    <h3>Where does a ban of five names land in activation space?</h3>
    <p class="q">When the five most common grid algorithms are banned by name, does the model move to an algorithm at the edge of the banned set or opposite it?</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-geo-ov">Prompt states drawn on the map</span>
        <div class="chips" role="group" aria-labelledby="lab-geo-ov" id="geo-ov"></div></div>
      <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-geo-pts">Forced prompts</span>
        <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-geo-pts" id="geo-pts"></div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart" id="geo-chart" role="group" aria-label="Activation-space map of ten grid algorithms"></div>
    <ul class="legend" id="geo-legend"></ul>
    <p class="takeaway" id="geo-take" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <p class="note">Points are the first two principal components of Qwen3-32B (4-bit weights, thinking mode) residual states at block <span data-k="geo_block"></span>, averaged over the task tokens of 300 forced <code>Implement &lt;algorithm&gt;</code> prompts (30 per algorithm); the axes carry <span data-k="geo_evr"></span> of the variance. Centroids are the means of each algorithm's points. Source: experiment 44, <code>results/geometry_M1.json</code>, <code>results/landing.json</code> and <code>data/labelled_C6_ban.jsonl</code>; program-map ratio from experiment 46, <code>results/geometry_32b_mcode_PRIMARY_R1.json</code>.</p>
  </div>
</div>
</section>

<!-- ============================== TRY IT ============================== -->
<section id="try" aria-labelledby="h-try">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-try">Try it: how hot would temperature have to be?</h2>
  <div class="card" id="wi-card">
    <p class="q">Temperature divides the logits by <i>T</i>. Given the recorded fork margin, how much of the output leaves the default at a temperature of your choosing?</p>
    <p class="small prose">The curve is the run's own two-token closed form, the share off the default when only the two leading fork tokens compete: 1 / (1 + e<sup><i>m</i>/<i>T</i></sup>) for a margin of <i>m</i> nats. It is a simplification the run recorded beside its fuller prediction over the top 20 fork tokens; both are drawn. It ignores the opening, so it is not the composed law.</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <div class="ctl"><label class="lab" for="wi-task">Task or unit</label><select id="wi-task"></select></div>
      <div class="ctl"><label class="lab" for="wi-T">Temperature <i>T</i>: <output class="valout" id="wi-Tout" for="wi-T"></output></label><input type="range" id="wi-T" min="0.1" max="3" step="0.05" value="1.3"></div>
      <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-wi-scale">Vertical scale</span>
        <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-wi-scale" id="wi-scale"></div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart" id="wi-chart" role="group" aria-label="Share off the default against temperature"></div>
    <ul class="legend" id="wi-legend"></ul>
    <p class="takeaway" id="wi-take" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <p class="note">Sources: experiment 35, <code>results/predictions_view.json</code> (margins, closed form and top-20 predictions; fork-token probabilities for the mixed units) and <code>results/test3.json</code> (samples drawn from the fork at <i>T</i> 1.3); observed shares of the mixed units from experiment 43, <code>results/analysis_L.json</code>.</p>
  </div>
</div>
</section>

<!-- ============================== FAILS ============================== -->
<section id="fails" aria-labelledby="h-fails">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-fails">Where it fails</h2>
  <div class="card">
    <h3>The law misses when the decision is spread over many openings</h3>
    <p class="q">Which unit does the composed law fail on, and why?</p>
    <p class="prose">On Llama-3.1-8B's grid task every predictor fails. Llama reaches the forking tokens through many openings, so the committed law is almost the flat law, and at high temperature the programs collapse into unusable code.</p>
    <p><button type="button" class="btn" id="fail-llama">Show the Llama grid unit in the law view</button></p>
    <p class="takeaway" id="fail-llama-take" aria-live="polite"></p>
  </div>
  <div class="card" id="ban-card">
    <h3>A ban of five names is mostly not obeyed</h3>
    <p class="q">Across ten open model configurations, how often does a ban of BFS, DFS, IDDFS, A* and greedy best-first by name yield a correct program that uses none of them?</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-ban-m">Measure</span>
        <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-ban-m" id="ban-m"></div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart" id="ban-chart" role="group" aria-label="Survivor share under a ban of five names, per configuration"></div>
    <p class="takeaway" id="ban-take" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <p class="note">A <button type="button" class="term" data-term="survivor">survivor</button> is a correct program whose algorithm is not banned. Whiskers are Wilson 95% intervals; the dashed line is the preregistered bar of <span data-k="ban_bar"></span>. Source: experiment 44, <code>results/screen.json</code>.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="card">
    <h3>What the paper does not show</h3>
    <ul class="limits prose">
      <li>The headline contrast between push and temperature ran only in an 8-bit (W8A8) engine. The push alone changes the algorithm in bfloat16 at the same absolute push norm, but the paired contrast was not repeated, and on the grid task the push moved only <span data-k="t1_a1"></span> of 20 seeds.</li>
      <li>Most results come from one model, Qwen3-8B, in non-thinking mode. The composed law was tested on <span data-k="law_heldout"></span> held-out units in two other families, below the four the preregistered claim required, so its generality is open.</li>
      <li>The law is not clearly better than the flat law, a baseline that predicts no change: it wins on <span data-k="law_vs_flat"></span> units (sign test <i>p</i> = <span data-k="law_sign_p"></span>). Much of its accuracy reflects how little temperature moves these units.</li>
      <li>The temperature null rests on 20 seeds per task, which bounds the change rate per seed below <span data-k="cp95"></span>, not at zero.</li>
      <li>The tasks are short, well-known problems whose solutions are probably memorised; conclusions may not carry to open-ended programs.</li>
      <li>Some label gates failed their strict criteria, so those numbers are descriptive. The activation-space geometry is correlational, and the map built from names is confounded by lexical overlap between algorithm names.</li>
      <li>No control the run tested produced a correct algorithm outside the known repertoire.</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
</section>
</main>

/*DATA*/
<script>
"use strict";
(function(){
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ data */
function J(id){return JSON.parse(document.getElementById(id).textContent);}
var SEEDS=J('data-seeds'), CODES=J('data-codes'), LAW=J('data-law'), STEP=J('data-stepper'), MARG=J('data-margins'),
    WHAT=J('data-whatif'), BAN=J('data-ban'), GEO=J('data-geom');

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers */
function fmt(x,d){ /* half-up rounding on the decimal value, as the paper prints */
  if(x===null||x===undefined||isNaN(x)) return '–';
  var neg=x<0, a=Math.abs(x), s=String(a);
  var r;
  if(s.indexOf('e')<0){ r=Number(Math.round(Number(s+'e'+d))+'e-'+d); }
  else { r=Number(a.toFixed(d)); }
  var out=r.toFixed(d);
  if(neg && Number(out)!==0) out='−'+out;
  return out;
}
function fmtSci(p,dig){
  if(p===0) return '0';
  var e=Math.floor(Math.log10(p)), m=p/Math.pow(10,e), ms=fmt(m,dig);
  if(Number(ms)>=10){e+=1; ms=fmt(m/10,dig);}
  return ms+' × 10<sup>−'+Math.abs(e)+'</sup>';
}
function pct(x){return fmt(100*x,0)+'%';}
var NS='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg';
function S(tag,attrs,parent){var e=document.createElementNS(NS,tag); if(attrs){for(var k in attrs){if(attrs[k]!==null&&attrs[k]!==undefined)e.setAttribute(k,attrs[k]);}} if(parent)parent.appendChild(e); return e;}
function T(parent,x,y,str,attrs){var t=S('text',Object.assign({x:x,y:y},attrs||{}),parent); t.textContent=str; return t;}
function H(tag,attrs,html){var e=document.createElement(tag); if(attrs){for(var k in attrs){if(k==='class')e.className=attrs[k]; else e.setAttribute(k,attrs[k]);}} if(html!==undefined)e.innerHTML=html; return e;}
function esc(s){return String(s).replace(/[&<>"]/g,function(c){return {'&':'&amp;','<':'&lt;','>':'&gt;','"':'&quot;'}[c];});}
var measurer=null;
function textW(str,size,weight){
  if(!measurer){measurer=S('svg',{width:0,height:0,style:'position:absolute;left:-9999px;top:0;visibility:hidden'}); document.body.appendChild(measurer);}
  var t=S('text',{'font-size':size,'font-weight':weight||400,'font-family':getComputedStyle(document.body).fontFamily},measurer); t.textContent=str;
  var w=t.getComputedTextLength(); measurer.removeChild(t); return w;
}
function niceTicks(lo,hi,n){var span=hi-lo, step=Math.pow(10,Math.floor(Math.log10(span/n))), err=n/span*step;
  if(err<=.15)step*=10; else if(err<=.35)step*=5; else if(err<=.75)step*=2;
  var a=Math.ceil(lo/step-1e-9)*step, out=[]; for(var v=a; v<=hi+1e-9; v+=step) out.push(Math.round(v/step)*step); return out;}
function ticksFmt(ticks){var st=ticks.length>1?Math.abs(ticks[1]-ticks[0]):1, d=st>=1?0:(st>=0.1?1:(st>=0.01?2:3)); return function(v){return fmt(v,d);};}
var NAME={dijkstra:'Dijkstra',bf_spfa:'Bellman-Ford/SPFA',other:'other (outside the catalogue)',full_sort:'full sort',quickselect:'quickselect',bfs:'BFS',dfs:'DFS'};
var LCOL={dijkstra:'#c5ced8',full_sort:'#c5ced8',bfs:'#c5ced8',bf_spfa:'#e69f00',quickselect:'#009e73',dfs:'#d55e00',other:'#cc79a7'};

/* tooltip for chart marks: opens on hover, focus and tap */
var tipEl=document.getElementById('marktip'), tipOwner=null;
function placeTip(el,box){var r=box||el.getBoundingClientRect(); tipEl.style.display='block';
  var tw=tipEl.offsetWidth, th=tipEl.offsetHeight, x=r.left+r.width/2-tw/2, y=r.top-th-10;
  if(y<8) y=r.bottom+10; x=Math.max(8,Math.min(window.innerWidth-tw-8,x)); tipEl.style.left=x+'px'; tipEl.style.top=y+'px';}
function showTip(el,html){tipOwner=el; tipEl.innerHTML=html; placeTip(el);}
function hideTip(){tipEl.style.display='none'; tipOwner=null;}
function mark(el,html,onAct){
  el.setAttribute('tabindex','0'); el.setAttribute('class',(el.getAttribute('class')||'')+' mark');
  el.setAttribute('role','img'); el.setAttribute('aria-label',html.replace(/<[^>]+>/g,''));
  el.addEventListener('pointerenter',function(){showTip(el,html);});
  el.addEventListener('pointerleave',function(){if(tipOwner===el)hideTip();});
  el.addEventListener('focus',function(){showTip(el,html);});
  el.addEventListener('blur',function(){if(tipOwner===el)hideTip();});
  el.addEventListener('click',function(ev){showTip(el,html); if(onAct)onAct(ev);});
  if(onAct) el.addEventListener('keydown',function(ev){if(ev.key==='Enter'||ev.key===' '){ev.preventDefault(); onAct(ev);}});
}
document.addEventListener('keydown',function(e){if(e.key==='Escape'){hideTip(); closeTerm();}});
document.addEventListener('pointerdown',function(e){if(tipOwner&&!tipOwner.contains(e.target))hideTip();});
window.addEventListener('scroll',function(){if(tipOwner)placeTip(tipOwner); if(termOwner)placeTerm(termOwner);},{passive:true});

/* segmented controls */
function seg(container,role,items,cur,onChange){
  container.innerHTML='';
  var btns=items.map(function(it,i){
    var b=H('button',{type:'button',role:role==='tablist'?'tab':'radio'},it.label);
    b.dataset.v=it.v; container.appendChild(b);
    b.addEventListener('click',function(){set(it.v,true);});
    b.addEventListener('keydown',function(e){var k=e.key, j=i;
      if(k==='ArrowRight'||k==='ArrowDown')j=(i+1)%items.length; else if(k==='ArrowLeft'||k==='ArrowUp')j=(i-1+items.length)%items.length; else return;
      e.preventDefault(); set(items[j].v,true); btns[j].focus();});
    return b;});
  function set(v,fire){btns.forEach(function(b){var on=b.dataset.v===String(v);
      b.setAttribute(role==='tablist'?'aria-selected':'aria-checked',on?'true':'false'); b.tabIndex=on?0:-1;});
    if(fire)onChange(v);}
  set(cur,false); return {set:set};
}
function chipToggle(container,items,isOn,onToggle){
  container.innerHTML='';
  items.forEach(function(it){var b=H('button',{type:'button','class':'chip','aria-pressed':isOn(it.v)?'true':'false'},it.label);
    if(it.title) b.setAttribute('aria-label',it.title);
    b.addEventListener('click',function(){var on=b.getAttribute('aria-pressed')!=='true'; b.setAttribute('aria-pressed',on?'true':'false'); onToggle(it.v,on);});
    container.appendChild(b);});
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ glossary and term tooltips */
var TERMS={
  crn:['Common random numbers','Every seed owns one stream of uniform variates, and every condition maps the same variates through its own next-token distribution, so a difference between two conditions on one seed is caused by the condition, not by a different draw.'],
  push:['Random task-state push','One isotropic unit direction added, during the prefill only, to the residual stream activations at the token positions that state the task, in blocks 12 to 23. Its size is set in multiples α of the displacement that a ban prompt induces at the same positions.'],
  spec:['Task specification states','The residual stream activations at the prompt tokens that state the task.'],
  fork:['Forking token','A position where resampling changes the algorithm distribution; found by resampling continuations from prefixes of growing length and refining the change point to a single token. "The fork" is short for the forking token.'],
  opening:['Shared opening','The common prefix that programs of different algorithms share before the forking token.'],
  margin:['Fork margin','The teacher-forced gap in log probability, at the forking token, between the class of tokens that lead to the default algorithm and the best class that leads elsewhere.'],
  law:['Composed law','A prediction of the algorithm distribution at temperature T built from the tempered probability of each shared opening, the tempered next-token distribution at the fork, and the share of each algorithm among continuations forced from each fork token. It uses only teacher-forced logits and T = 1 conditionals, so it can be committed before any temperature sample.'],
  flat:['Flat law','A rival that keeps the T = 1 shares at every temperature: a baseline that predicts no change.'],
  mae:['Mean absolute error (MAE)','The mean over the four temperatures of the total variation distance between predicted and observed label distributions.'],
  unit:['Unit','A task paired with one model. A default task is one where the instruct model writes one algorithm in essentially all samples; a mixed unit already contains a second algorithm at a share of roughly 0.1 to 0.4.'],
  exchange:['Task-state exchange','The task specification states of a forced prompt ("Implement the task with <minority algorithm>") are written into the forward pass of a padding twin, a copy in which the instruction is replaced by padding tokens so that all positions align.'],
  phrasing:['Phrasing cluster','A connected component, within one idea, of programs whose AST 4-gram shingle sets (identifiers normalised; comments, docstrings and constants dropped) have Jaccard similarity at least 0.8.'],
  idea:['Idea','The runtime label of a correct program.'],
  change:['Change count','For a block of conditions, the number of seeds whose algorithm label differs anywhere across the block.'],
  survivor:['Survivor','A correct program whose algorithm is not banned.'],
  ban5:['Ban of five names','An instruction not to use five named algorithms at once (here BFS, DFS, IDDFS, A* and greedy best-first search).'],
  landing:['Landing','The algorithm a changed program moved to.'],
  hclass:['H(A | class)','The entropy of the algorithm given the class of the forking token: how much uncertainty about the algorithm remains once the fork token is known.']
};
var gloss=document.getElementById('gloss'), defs=document.getElementById('term-defs');
Object.keys(TERMS).forEach(function(k){
  gloss.appendChild(H('dt',{id:'gl-'+k},esc(TERMS[k][0]))); gloss.appendChild(H('dd',null,esc(TERMS[k][1])));
  defs.appendChild(H('span',{id:'def-'+k},esc(TERMS[k][0])+': '+esc(TERMS[k][1])));
});
var termTip=document.getElementById('termtip'), termOwner=null;
function placeTerm(el){var r=el.getBoundingClientRect(); termTip.style.display='block'; var tw=termTip.offsetWidth, th=termTip.offsetHeight;
  var x=Math.max(8,Math.min(window.innerWidth-tw-8,r.left)), y=r.bottom+8; if(y+th>window.innerHeight-8) y=r.top-th-8; termTip.style.left=x+'px'; termTip.style.top=y+'px';}
function openTerm(el){var k=el.dataset.term; if(!TERMS[k])return; if(termOwner&&termOwner!==el)termOwner.setAttribute('aria-expanded','false');
  termOwner=el; el.setAttribute('aria-expanded','true'); termTip.innerHTML='<b>'+esc(TERMS[k][0])+'.</b> '+esc(TERMS[k][1]); placeTerm(el);}
function closeTerm(){if(termOwner)termOwner.setAttribute('aria-expanded','false'); termOwner=null; termTip.style.display='none';}
function wireTerm(el){var k=el.dataset.term; el.setAttribute('aria-describedby','def-'+k); el.setAttribute('aria-expanded','false');
  ['mouseenter','focus','click'].forEach(function(ev){el.addEventListener(ev,function(){openTerm(el);});});
  el.addEventListener('mouseleave',function(){if(termOwner===el && document.activeElement!==el)closeTerm();});
  el.addEventListener('blur',function(){if(termOwner===el)closeTerm();});}
document.querySelectorAll('.term').forEach(wireTerm);
document.addEventListener('pointerdown',function(e){if(termOwner&&!termOwner.contains(e.target))closeTerm();});

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ 1. headline: seeds x conditions */
var hl={task:'T2',temp:'temp',alpha:'1.0',dirs:{1:true,2:true,3:true,4:false,5:false,6:false}};
var TASKNAME={T2:'Shortest path',T03:'k-th smallest',T1:'Grid path'};
function rowsOf(task){return SEEDS.rows[task];}
function lab(cell){return cell?SEEDS.labels[cell[0]]:null;}
function tempCols(){return (hl.temp==='think'?['THINK_T0.3','THINK_T0.7','THINK_T1.0','THINK_T1.3']:['NOPN_T0.3','NOPN_T0.7','NOPN_T1.0','NOPN_T1.3']);}
function pushCols(){var a=[]; for(var d=1;d<=6;d++)a.push('PN_D4600'+d+'_a'+hl.alpha+'_T1.0'); return a;}
function changedTemp(row){var ls={}, n=0; tempCols().forEach(function(c){var x=lab(row.cells[c]); if(x!==null){ls[x]=1;n++;}}); return n===0?null:Object.keys(ls).length>1;}
function changedPush(row){var base=lab(row.cells['NOPN_T1.0']), any=false, sel=0; for(var d=1;d<=6;d++){if(!hl.dirs[d])continue; sel++; var x=lab(row.cells['PN_D4600'+d+'_a'+hl.alpha+'_T1.0']); if(x!==null&&x!==base)any=true;} return sel?any:null;}
function condLabel(c){
  if(c.indexOf('NOPN_T')===0) return 'temperature '+c.slice(6)+', thinking off'+(c==='NOPN_T1.0'?' (also the unpushed arm)':'');
  if(c.indexOf('THINK_T')===0) return 'temperature '+c.slice(7)+', thinking on';
  if(c==='TOPK10_T0.7') return 'top-k 10 at temperature 0.7';
  if(c==='MINP_T2.0') return 'min-p 0.1 at temperature 2.0';
  var m=c.match(/PN_D4600(\d)_a([\d.]+)_T1\.0/); if(m) return 'push direction '+m[1]+', α = '+Number(m[2])+', T 1.0';
  return c;}
function drawMatrix(){
  var box=document.getElementById('hl-matrix'); box.innerHTML='';
  var rows=rowsOf(hl.task), W=Math.max(300,box.clientWidth), tc=tempCols(), pc=pushCols();
  var labW=Math.ceil(textW('W5·3',12))+10, markW=34, gap=16, top=46;
  var cw=Math.max(14,Math.min(46,(W-labW-gap-markW*2-6)/10)), ch=Math.max(13,Math.min(18,cw*0.62));
  var w=labW+cw*4+gap+cw*6+markW*2+6, h=top+ch*rows.length+8;
  var svg=S('svg',{viewBox:'0 0 '+w+' '+h,width:w,height:h},box); svg.style.maxWidth=w+'px';
  var x0=labW, x1=labW+cw*4+gap;
  T(svg,x0,13,hl.temp==='think'?'Temperature, thinking on':'Temperature, thinking off',{'font-size':12,'font-weight':650});
  T(svg,x1,13,'Push, α = '+Number(hl.alpha)+', T 1.0',{'font-size':12,'font-weight':650});
  ['0.3','0.7','1.0','1.3'].forEach(function(t,i){T(svg,x0+cw*i+cw/2,34,t,{'font-size':11,'text-anchor':'middle'});});
  for(var d=1;d<=6;d++){T(svg,x1+cw*(d-1)+cw/2,34,'d'+d,{'font-size':11,'text-anchor':'middle','font-weight':hl.dirs[d]?700:400,fill:hl.dirs[d]?'#1b2029':'#9aa3ae'});}
  T(svg,x1+cw*6+markW/2+3,34,'push',{'font-size':10,'text-anchor':'middle'});
  T(svg,x0+cw*4+gap/2,34,'',{});
  T(svg,x1-gap/2,h-2,'',{});
  rows.forEach(function(row,r){
    var y=top+r*ch;
    var cT=changedTemp(row), cP=changedPush(row);
    T(svg,labW-6,y+ch*0.72,row.w+'·'+row.i,{'font-size':11,'text-anchor':'end',fill:cP?'#1d5bbf':'#5f6878','font-weight':cP?700:400});
    function cell(c,x,dim){
      var v=row.cells[c];
      if(!v){var g=S('rect',{x:x+1,y:y+1,width:cw-2,height:ch-2,fill:'#fff',stroke:'#d5d9de','stroke-dasharray':'2 2'},svg);
        mark(g,'<b>Seed '+row.w+'·'+row.i+'</b>, '+condLabel(c)+': not run'); return;}
      var l=SEEDS.labels[v[0]], g2=S('g',{'class':'cellr',opacity:dim?0.22:1},svg);
      S('rect',{x:x+1,y:y+1,width:cw-2,height:ch-2,rx:2,fill:LCOL[l]||'#999'},g2);
      if(!v[1]) S('rect',{x:x+cw/2-3,y:y+ch/2-3,width:6,height:6,fill:'#fff',stroke:'#1b2029','stroke-width':1},g2);
      mark(g2,'<b>Seed '+row.w+'·'+row.i+'</b>, '+condLabel(c)+'<br>Algorithm: <b>'+esc(NAME[l]||l)+'</b><br>'+(v[1]?'Passes':'Fails')+' the hidden tests',function(){openInBrowser(hl.task,c,row);});
    }
    tc.forEach(function(c,i){cell(c,x0+cw*i,false);});
    pc.forEach(function(c,i){cell(c,x1+cw*i,!hl.dirs[i+1]);});
    if(cP) {var mk=S('text',{x:x1+cw*6+markW/2+3,y:y+ch*0.74,'text-anchor':'middle','font-size':11,'font-weight':700,fill:'#1d5bbf'},svg); mk.textContent='changed';}
  });
  var lg=document.getElementById('hl-legend'); lg.innerHTML='';
  var present={}; rows.forEach(function(row){tc.concat(pc).forEach(function(c){var v=row.cells[c]; if(v)present[SEEDS.labels[v[0]]]=1;});});
  Object.keys(present).forEach(function(l){lg.appendChild(H('li',null,'<span class="sw" style="background:'+LCOL[l]+'"></span>'+esc(NAME[l]||l)+(['dijkstra','full_sort','bfs'].indexOf(l)>=0?' (the task default)':'')));});
  lg.appendChild(H('li',null,'<span class="sw" style="background:#fff;border:1px solid #1b2029;width:9px;height:9px;border-radius:1px"></span>small white square: fails the hidden tests'));
  lg.appendChild(H('li',null,'<span class="sw" style="background:#fff;border:1px dashed #a0a7b1"></span>not run'));
}
function drawBars(){
  var box=document.getElementById('hl-bars'); box.innerHTML='';
  var rows=rowsOf(hl.task), st=ST[hl.task], W=Math.max(300,box.clientWidth);
  var nTemp=0, nTempCount=0, nTempMax=0; rows.forEach(function(r){var c=changedTemp(r); if(c!==null){nTempMax++; if(c)nTemp++;}});
  var nThinkRows=0, nThink=0; rows.forEach(function(r){var ls={},n=0; ['THINK_T0.3','THINK_T0.7','THINK_T1.0','THINK_T1.3'].forEach(function(c){var x=lab(r.cells[c]); if(x!==null){ls[x]=1;n++;}}); if(n===4){nThinkRows++; if(Object.keys(ls).length>1)nThink++;}});
  var sel=0; for(var d=1;d<=6;d++) if(hl.dirs[d]) sel++;
  var nSel=0; rows.forEach(function(r){if(changedPush(r))nSel++;});
  var items=[
    {lab:'Temperature 0.3, 0.7, 1.0, 1.3, top-p 1',v:st.temp_change,c:'#8b95a4',note:st.temp_change+' of 20'},
    {lab:'The same, plus top-k 10 at T 0.7',v:st.with_topk,c:'#8b95a4',note:st.with_topk+' of 20'},
    {lab:'The same, plus min-p 0.1 at T 2.0',v:st.with_minp,c:'#8b95a4',note:st.with_minp+' of 20'},
    {lab:'Temperature 0.3 to 1.3, thinking mode',v:nThinkRows?nThink:null,c:'#8b95a4',note:nThinkRows?(nThink+' of '+nThinkRows):'not run',max:nThinkRows},
    {lab:'Push α = 1: mean over the 20 subsets of three directions (min to max)',v:st['a1.0'].mean,lo:st['a1.0'].min,hi:st['a1.0'].max,c:'#7fa6dd',note:fmt(st['a1.0'].mean,2)+' of 20'},
    {lab:'Push α = 2: mean over the 20 subsets of three directions (min to max)',v:st['a2.0'].mean,lo:st['a2.0'].min,hi:st['a2.0'].max,c:'#1d5bbf',note:fmt(st['a2.0'].mean,2)+' of 20'},
    {lab:'Push α = '+Number(hl.alpha)+', the '+sel+' direction'+(sel===1?'':'s')+' you selected',v:sel?nSel:null,c:'#e69f00',note:sel?(nSel+' of 20'):'select a direction'}
  ];
  var padL=4, padR=Math.ceil(textW('19.05 of 20',12,700))+12, bh=14, rowH=40, top=6, axisH=40;
  var h=top+items.length*rowH+axisH, x0=padL, x1=W-padR, sx=function(v){return x0+(x1-x0)*v/20;};
  var svg=S('svg',{viewBox:'0 0 '+W+' '+h,width:W,height:h},box);
  [0,5,10,15,20].forEach(function(t){S('line',{x1:sx(t),x2:sx(t),y1:top,y2:h-axisH+4,stroke:'#eef0f2'},svg); T(svg,sx(t),h-axisH+18,String(t),{'font-size':11,'text-anchor':'middle'});});
  T(svg,(x0+x1)/2,h-6,'Seeds whose algorithm changed (of 20)',{'font-size':12,'text-anchor':'middle','font-weight':600});
  items.forEach(function(it,i){
    var y=top+i*rowH;
    T(svg,x0,y+12,it.lab,{'font-size':11.5,fill:'#3f4756'});
    var by=y+17;
    S('rect',{x:x0,y:by,width:x1-x0,height:bh,fill:'#f4f5f7'},svg);
    if(it.v!==null&&it.v!==undefined){
      var r=S('rect',{'class':'bar',x:x0,y:by,width:Math.max(0,sx(it.v)-x0),height:bh,fill:it.c},svg);
      if(it.lo!==undefined){S('line',{x1:sx(it.lo),x2:sx(it.hi),y1:by+bh/2,y2:by+bh/2,stroke:'#1b2029','stroke-width':1.5},svg);
        S('line',{x1:sx(it.lo),x2:sx(it.lo),y1:by+2,y2:by+bh-2,stroke:'#1b2029','stroke-width':1.5},svg); S('line',{x1:sx(it.hi),x2:sx(it.hi),y1:by+2,y2:by+bh-2,stroke:'#1b2029','stroke-width':1.5},svg);}
      var hit=S('rect',{x:x0,y:by-3,width:x1-x0,height:bh+6,fill:'transparent'},svg);
      mark(hit,'<b>'+esc(it.lab)+'</b><br>'+esc(it.note)+(it.lo!==undefined?' (subsets range '+it.lo+' to '+it.hi+')':''));
    }
    T(svg,x1+6,by+bh-2,it.note,{'font-size':12,'font-weight':700,fill:'#1b2029'});
  });
  var tn=TASKNAME[hl.task], landing={};
  rows.forEach(function(r){var base=lab(r.cells['NOPN_T1.0']); for(var d=1;d<=6;d++){if(!hl.dirs[d])continue; var x=lab(r.cells['PN_D4600'+d+'_a'+hl.alpha+'_T1.0']); if(x&&x!==base)landing[x]=(landing[x]||0)+1;}});
  var lands=Object.keys(landing).sort(function(a,b){return landing[b]-landing[a];}).map(function(k){return NAME[k]+' ('+landing[k]+')';});
  var tk=document.getElementById('hl-take');
  var tempTxt=(hl.temp==='think'?(nThinkRows?('With thinking on, temperature changed '+nThink+' of '+nThinkRows+' seeds'):'Thinking mode was not run on this task, but with thinking off temperature changed '+nTemp+' of '+nTempMax+' seeds'):('Temperature changed '+nTemp+' of '+nTempMax+' seeds'));
  tk.textContent= tn+': '+tempTxt+'. '+(sel?('The union of the '+sel+' selected push direction'+(sel===1?'':'s')+' at α = '+Number(hl.alpha)+' changed '+nSel+' of 20'+(lands.length?(', and the changed programs landed on '+lands.join(', ')+'.'):'.')):'Select at least one push direction to compare.');
}

seg(document.getElementById('hl-task'),'tablist',SEEDS.tasks.map(function(t){return {v:t.id,label:t.name};}),hl.task,function(v){hl.task=v; drawHeadline();});
